label: Jul 16 – 30, 2026
period_mismatch_note: This is a 15-day report generated for the client review. It is compared like-for-like against the prior 15-day fortnight (Jul 1–15), so every delta is a fair fortnight-over-fortnight figure. Note the prior fortnight (Jul 1–15) was an exceptionally strong first half; across all of July the program produced roughly 112 leads, holding the record pace of the prior month.
cadence_note: The regular cadence is a 30-day report; this fortnight snapshot was produced on request for the client meeting.

summary.narrative: A deliberately lighter-spend fortnight that capped a strong July, with the operational wins landing where they matter most. Paid spend was pulled back 39% to $10.4K, and the standout result is on the phone: the answer rate reached 88% (7 of 8 calls) with answered calls up 40% — the single issue flagged as red for three straight periods is now resolved. Search continued to do the heavy lifting and got more efficient: Google's cost per lead improved 18% to $477 and branded search converted at a 43% click-through rate. Site visitors grew 25% to 5.4K and organic position improved from 14.5 to 12.9. The one area to keep watching is lead volume: this half produced 38 leads against an exceptional 74 in the first two weeks of the month, as Meta normalized from a standout run and Display scaled to 1.2M impressions — lifting traffic while diluting blended efficiency. Across all of July the program delivered roughly 112 leads, in line with the record pace. The warm bench is healthy at 23, with two reservation holders and six sales visits in motion.

website_organic.engagement_highlight: The Residences page held a 7.7% bounce rate with 2:08 average time, and the Broker Toolkit averaged nearly 6 minutes — the deep-intent pages are performing.

recommendations.headline: Phone coverage is fixed — lock in the gain
recommendations.detail: The answer rate reached 88% (7 of 8 calls) with answered calls up 40%, resolving the issue flagged red for three straight reports. Only one call was missed. Keep the backup ring group and voicemail follow-up in place so this holds as call volume rebuilds — every answered call from paid search is worth protecting.

recommendations.headline: Cap and geo-tighten Display before it distorts the account
recommendations.detail: Display scaled to 1.23 million impressions for $2,293 and one tracked conversion, and it is the reason the blended Google conversion rate reads 0.41% while site visitors rose 25%. Search, by contrast, converted 13 leads at a $332 cost per lead. Tighten geo and placements to Sarasota plus genuine feeder markets, cap the budget, and judge Display on form fills and assisted conversions rather than raw reach.

recommendations.headline: Rebuild Meta volume around Brochure Download
recommendations.detail: Meta leads normalized to 24 from an exceptional 54 in the first half, and cost per lead rose to $154. Brochure Download remains the efficient engine — 10 leads at $65 — while Feeder Market Segmented ran $198 per lead. Shift budget back toward Brochure Download and Sarasota prospecting to bring the blended Meta cost per lead back under $120.

recommendations.headline: Keep the Microsoft/Bing channel in view
recommendations.detail: Microsoft paid search delivered 524 sessions (468 non-branded, 56 branded) plus one CallRail 'Bing Ads' call, but still has no cost or conversion data in this dashboard. Confirm the spend and add the source so its true cost per lead is visible alongside Google and Meta.

recommendations.headline: Decide on Competitors: 1.5 conversions for $1,235
recommendations.detail: The Competitors campaign converted at roughly $823 per lead against a blended $273. Either trim it to a small brand-defense budget or move the money to Non-Brand Sarasota and Branded Search, which together produced 11.5 conversions far more efficiently.

recommendations.headline: Clear the Miramar-Florida mix-up in search
recommendations.detail: Roughly 425 organic impressions again came from Miramar, FL apartment and property-management searches with zero clicks — the biggest single drag on average position, which nonetheless improved to 12.9. Add negatives on the paid side and keep publishing Sarasota-anchored content to push position toward single digits.

recommendations.headline: Work the warm bench — 23 warm, buyers progressing
recommendations.detail: The warm count sits at 23 with two reservation holders and six sales visits or meetings in motion, and four new agent registrations arrived this period. Named buyers are advancing: Elizabeth Gomez (relocating builder, ~$4M, reviewing units 702 and 705), Ken Rollyson and Michael Williams Jones (both local, long-lead), and Gail Trippi. These are the relationships most likely to convert to reservations next quarter.
